verdict.rationale: Cursor's own docs cover headless and CI use of the CLI in detail. Print mode (-p) is documented for non-interactive scripts and CI, with --force to apply edits and CURSOR_API_KEY auth. There is a GitHub Actions install-and-run recipe, machine-readable json/stream-json output with non-zero exit codes on failure, and service accounts recommended for CI and cron. missing for 10: independent hands-on or community corroboration of headless/CI runs.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can run the product headlessly / in CI for automation

citations.quote: Use print mode for non-interactive scenarios like scripts, CI pipelines, or automation
Use Cursor CLI in GitHub Actions and other CI/CD systems to automate development tasks.
Use print mode (`-p, --print`) for non-interactive scripting and automation
This is the recommended way to run the CLI in CI/CD pipelines, cron jobs, and other non-interactive environments.
On failure, the process exits with a non-zero code and writes an error message to stderr.
